title: Prescriptions Schedule of Continuity Days on Strength-Error Remakes
content:
Under Kestrel Prescriptions, a strength-error remake carries continuity days when the prescription has few or no refills left, so that therapy is bridged.

## Schedule

The strength-error continuity allowance looks at the refills left on the prescription, being the refills the prescriber authorized less the refills used by its refills plus the refills restored by returns to stock:

| Refills left | Continuity days |
|---|---|
| none (0 or fewer) | 5 |
| exactly 1 | 3 |
| 2 or more | 0 |

Each continuity day adds the prescribed daily units — the prescription's written quantity divided by its written days supply — to the strength-error remake quantity.

## Worked readings (hypothetical ledger)

| Refills authorized | Refills used by refills | Refills restored by returns to stock | Refills left | Continuity days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 5 |
| 5 | 5 | 1 | 1 | 3 |
| 5 | 4 | 0 | 1 | 3 |
| 5 | 3 | 0 | 2 | 0 |

With 3 prescribed daily units, 5 continuity days add 15 units and 3 continuity days add 9 units.

**Which refill count is used?** The count worked out from the authorized refills and the fill ledger as above.
